name: Priest — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Priest from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's pages "The Priest", "Priest" but are not part of the Priest entry, which is unchanged.

From d20pfsrd.com: The Priest

Every society has its oracles, shamans, and holy men. Seers and prophets, ministers and yogis serve the masses in times of hardship and need.

They are community leaders, advisors, and shepherds. Priests are also advocates of their deity’s agenda in this world, fighting for influence and followers.

Priests work within the communities to change hearts and minds through peaceful means, while militant holy warriors such as paladins and clerics venture abroad to further the goals of the gods on the remote frontiers and on bloody battlefields. Priests strengthen and spread the influence of their deity by guiding, advising, and protecting the members of their flock. Although they are not warriors, many priests are powerful adversaries of undead and demons. They are also mighty healers, commanding more magic than any cleric of similar skill.

However, not all priests are agents of benevolence and charity. Evil priests abound. Hurling curses and destroying life, they follow wicked gods and malevolent philosophies. These ministers of darkness raise armies of undead and summon demons to plague mankind.

Priests are often revered among the lay people whom they shepherd and they act as intermediaries for the gods, guiding people through the troubles of daily life. Priests also provide council to powerful political leaders and sometimes take the reins of government themselves.

Adventures: Priests see the challenges of adventure as tests of faith. While not as interested in personal gain as other characters might be, priests are still motivated by a desire to increase the power and influence of the organizations they represent. They are also extremely vigilant about protecting their valued faith from destructive forces.

Characteristics: Priests spend much of their time in study and contemplation, researching and communing with their gods. They are also intimately involved in performing the rites of the temple and guiding the flock. Priests often outrank clerics and paladins in the temple hierarchy, and spend more of their time delegating tasks and supervising projects. Priests are very close to their gods and intimately familiar with their philosophical dogma. They can cast divine spells and have several innate abilities similar to those of bards, which they can use to influence their followers and affect their enemies.

Alignment: Priests can be of any alignment. However, the priest’s alignment cannot be more than one step removed from the alignment of their deity. For example, a priest that follows a Lawful Good god is usually also Lawful Good, but could be Lawful Neutral or Neutral Good.

Religion: Faith is the most important thing to a priest. And priests are often the most important things to a religion. A priest lives by the code and scripture outlined by his faith and works to preserve and promote it. Although most priests devote themselves to a deity or divine power, some devote themselves to causes or philosophies.

Background: Most priests joined the religious fold early in life, though there are some who don’t begin their studies until later. The early years of a priest’s studies are spent as a student and assistant. In their teen years they begin to acquire a certain amount of responsibility and begin studying abstract concepts and higher contemplation. Upon reaching adulthood, they either go on to postgraduate study, work as scribes, clerks, and bookkeepers, or they are dispatched to various parishes to minister to the flock. Sometimes they are sent to remote parishes or even into lands of nonbelievers to spread the message of their faith. Other times they are sent to large urban centers, serving as one of several low ranking minions in a large temple.

Other Characters: Priests work closely with clerics, monks, and paladins of their own faith. They also work occasionally with fighters and rogues. However, some priests dislike wizards and regard them as demon worshipers. Priests often contribute their skills in diplomacy, healing, and divine guidance to a group of adventurers.

Priests have the following game statistics.

Abilities: Wisdom determines how powerful a spell a priest can cast, how many spells he can cast, and how hard those spells are to resist. To cast a spell, a priest must have a Wisdom score of 10 + the spell’s level. In addition, priests gain bonus spells based on Wisdom. Charisma is also an important skill for priests, as it affects how many times per day he may channel energy, and how much healing his lay hands ability provides.

Prognostication (Ex)

All Priests are skilled in some form of Prognostication or fortune telling. Depending on their religion, they may use horoscopy, cartomancy, or another form of divination. See the appendix for details.

Convert (Ex)

Priests of 2nd level and higher can perform a simple ritual that will admit a new follower to their religion.

Excommunicate (Ex)

Priest of 2nd level and higher can, with appropriate cause, expel a follower from their faith, thereby preventing them from receiving any beneficial spells cast by any priest of that religion.

Excommunicating someone without proper cause can have negative repercussions for the priest, should the excommunicated person somehow manage to have his grievance heard and addressed by a higher power.

Excommunications can also be reversed though performing atonement.

Cohort (Ex)

Zealot (Ex)

Upon reaching 12th level, priests acquire a fanatical follower who blindly obeys their directions. The level and class of this zealot are determined with the rules regarding the Leadership feat, except that the zealot believes the priest has a reputation of great renown and a special power (total +3 Leadership bonus). The zealot is also always of the same alignment and religion as the priest. If the priest has caused the death of a previous zealot, sycophant, or cohort, it does not negatively affect his Leadership score when attracting a zealot. Any followers indicated by the priest’s Leadership score also accompany the zealot.

A zealot cannot be turned against his leader with suggestion and similar spells and spell-like abilities of 4th level or less. Zealots also gain a second saving throw if affected by dominate person, dominate monster, or similar mind effecting affects and compelled to work against their leader.

Zealots will also endure a great deal of mistreatment and abuse from their leader before they consider abandoning him.

Prognostication Skill Unlock

Priests and wizards gain the prognostication skill unlock at 1st level. Wizards may choose any method of divination, but priests are restricted to the methods traditionally used by their religion. Fate priests use horoscopy, priests of dualism use cartomancy, light priests use pyromancy, and cultist often use extispicy or osteomancy.

Prognostication (Sense Motive)

From d20pfsrd.com: Priest

Within the echoing halls of every grand cathedral are clergymen orchestrating the miracles of their praised and beloved deity. While most of these holy men are content with the life behind a podium, some don their simple robes and venture into the world of adventure as a hand of their god. Whether these priests bring peace, disorder, healing, or corruption upon the land depends on the forces that grant them their awesome power. Priests live and die by their god’s dogmas.

Role: A priest often stays near the back in the party, healing the injured from afar and blasting enemies from even farther away. A priest’s dogma heavily influences her spellcasting style, blessing her with the power to buff her allies, control the battlefield, or destroy her foes. Like a cleric, all priests must focus their worship upon a divine source. While the vast majority of priests revere a specific deity, a small number dedicate themselves to an abstract concept worthy of devotion—such as battle, death, justice, or knowledge—free of deific abstraction. (Work with your GM if you prefer this path to selecting a specific deity.)

Ability Scores: A priest’s spells rely on Wisdom. Channel energy and many of her dogma powers are based on Charisma. And such is the case for every adventurer, a good Constitution is important.

Her dogma grants a dogma power, dependent upon the level of the priest, as well as a number of bonus spells that a priest adds to her list of spells known. Unless otherwise noted, activating a dogma power is a standard action.

Primary Dogma Power: A priest gains the granted power of her selected primary dogma.

Religious Study

Starting at 2nd level, a priest gains a bonus on Knowledge (arcana), Knowledge (religion), and another Knowledge of her choice (reflecting the focus of her deity) and Linguistics skill checks equal to half of her priest level (rounded down). In addition, she may make these Knowledge and Linguistics skill checks untrained.

Secondary Dogmas

At 2nd level, a priest selects two more dogmas that function the same as her primary dogma except that the bonus spells from her secondary dogmas are granted a level later than her primary dogma spells, i.e. she gains her bonus 1st level spells at level 2, 2nd level spells at level 4, 3rd level spells and level 6, and so on.

Secondary Dogma Powers: At 4th level, a priest gains the granted powers of her selected secondary dogmas.

Enlightenment

At 20th level, a priest discovers the ultimate truths in all of her deity’s dogmas, not just the three that she has rigorously studied. At the beginning of each day, a priest may change her selected dogmas to three others that she qualifies for.

Humans: Add +1/4 uses of channel energy. (Every 4 times this is selected, gain an extra use of channel energy)
Dogmas

A priest can select any dogma granted by her deity. And at 2nd level, she chooses two more. Deities grant dogmas of the same name as the domains they grant. A priest without a deity may select any three dogmas (subject to GM approval). If a dogma’s power duplicates a spell effect, the priest’s caster level for that power is equal to her priest level.

Subdogmas are listed under their associated dogma. Subdogmas may have different powers and spells than their associated dogma. A priest may select both a dogma and its corresponding subdogmas; however, granted powers do not stack.

Archetypes
